Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. Let's see what Pakistan say about this pitch. Acceptable? Fakhar Zaman and Saim Ayub are the openers for the visiting side. Mahedi Hasan will start things off to Fakhar. Here we go.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Heading into the second innings, all eyes now shift to how Pakistan handle this chase. The pitch has been misbehaving, where some balls have got stepped bounce, and stroke-making isn’t as easy. Bangladesh will be hopeful, as they’ve got a decent bowling unit that can extract out of this wicket if they strike early. The key for Pakistan will be to build partnerships and not throw wickets under pressure. Join us in a bit for the chase!

Pakistan’s bowling was overall sharp and smart. Salman Mirza, yet again, led the charge with pace, control, and a maiden over to his name along with two wickets. Ahmed Daniyal on debut looked impressive too, taking two wickets and maintaining pressure. Nawaz and Faheem were both tidy, chipping in with crucial strikes at the right moments. Abbas Afridi was a touch expensive at the end, going for 37 in under four overs, mostly due to Jaker’s late blitz. Pakistan also shuffled through seven bowlers. Their fielding was good for the most part, with a direct hit and some sharp work, though they did spill a chance. Despite the late leak, they would still fancy their chances chasing 134.

For Bangladesh, it was a collapse that mirrored panic more than pressure. Mohammad Naim went for a scoop, Litton Das tried to force one too many, and Tawhid Hridoy got run out on his call only. In no time, they were four down inside six overs. It needed calm heads, and Jaker found some support in Mahedi Hasan. Together, they stitched the only meaningful partnership of the innings, 53 runs that slowed the collapse and provided a platform to at least aim for respectability. Mahedi injected momentum with some timely boundaries before falling while going for glory. Jaker, though, stayed till the end, launched five sixes, and ensured Bangladesh finished with some runs to bowl at. His 55 off 48 was necessary for survival.

Bangladesh have finished their innings at 133, a total that looked far-fetched when they were tumbling early in the Powerplay. It’s not a big score by any means, but given the pitch conditions, this might just be enough to create pressure. Things looked grim at 28/4, with the top order falling, where there were everything from careless shots to poor judgement, and a moment of brilliance in the field from Salman Agha made it worse. But from that shambles, rose a gritty fifty from Jaker Ali, whose fightback and six-hitting display in the final overs breathed life into the innings. Pakistan, meanwhile, dominated for the most part, using the conditions perfectly. However, their grip loosened a bit in the final five overs, where they conceded 47 runs, which could come back to haunt them if the chase gets tricky.

Commentary.Commentary: Right. The players take their respective positions. The lone star for Pakistan in the past match - Salman Mirza - will start off with the new ball.  Mohammad Naim and Parvez Hossain Emon are the openers for Bangladesh. Naim to face. Here we go!

A bit of a sombre mood in Dhaka today. There was an air crash tragedy which took place on Monday and has left the entire nation in shock. As a mark of respect, the players and officials are observing a minute's silence. Just for the details - A Bangladesh Air Force training jet crashed into the campus of Milestone School and College in Dhaka on Monday, killing at least 19 people and injuring over 160 others.  The incident occurred shortly after the aircraft took off from the Kurmitola Air Base, with the pilot making an attempt to divert the plane away from densely populated areas. May their souls rest in peace and the Almighty give their families strength to survive this period.

Meanwhile, in Harare, in a dead-rubber final league match between South Africa and New Zealand in Harare, meeting for the second time in the triseries, South Africa have been reduced to 57/4 in the 11th over. Once again, the Kiwi bowlers have been on point, not giving anything to the new-look African team. With Zimbabwe already knocked out, the last two matches of the league stage will prove as a sort of warmup games for the two finalists - New Zealand and South Africa.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Saim Ayub, Mohammad Haris (WK), Salman Agha (C), Hasan Nawaz, Mohammad Nawaz, Khushdil Shah, Faheem Ashraf, Abbas Afridi, Ahmed Daniyal (On T20I Debut and in place of Abrar Ahmed) and Salman Mirza.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (C) (WK), Parvez Hossain Emon, Mohammad Naim (In place of Tanzid Hasan), Tawhid Hridoy, Jaker Ali, Shamim Hossain, Mahedi Hasan, Rishad Hossain, Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam (In place of Taskin Ahmed) and Tanzim Hasan Sakib.
TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.

As for the conditions, the pitch will again be under scrutiny. Expect another slow, two-paced surface, with early showers in the forecast that could briefly interrupt play. Stay tuned for more updates!

Bangladesh, meanwhile, have quietly strung together an impressive turnaround. Parvez Hossain Emon continues to dazzle, anchoring the chase with a 56 not out in the first game, while Tawhid Hridoy and Taskin Ahmed provided solid support with bat and ball, respectively. Mustafizur Rahman’s magical spell of 2 for 6 was another reminder of his class. Even with Litton and Tanzid failing early, the rest of the batting stood up, a sign of a side that’s growing in depth and belief. They dropped a couple of chances in the field, which they need to look out for - otherwise, they just need to repeat what they did in the first game and will clinch the series.

For Pakistan, this is about damage control and rediscovering their rhythm. Fakhar Zaman looked good with a 34-ball 44, but a costly miscommunication cut his innings short. Apart from Abbas Afridi's cameo, no one else managed to cross 20. The batting order seemed unsure, and the absence of their pace trio, Shaheen, Haris, and Naseem, has made the attack look toothless, though Salman Mirza offered a silver lining with two early wickets. But Pakistan can’t afford another brittle display, as their young top order needs to shoulder responsibility and adapt to these trickier surfaces.

In the opener, Bangladesh produced a clinical all-round performance to chase down 110 in just 15.3 overs, but the pitch controversy stole headlines. Pakistan coach Mike Hesson labelled it ‘unacceptable for international cricket’, questioning the surface's role in their collapse. But it wasn’t just the pitch, as Pakistan's batting effort left plenty to be desired. They made a below-par total, and Bangladesh’s calm showed which team had more control under pressure.

Hello and welcome to the Shere Bangla National Stadium in Dhaka for the second T20I between Bangladesh and Pakistan, a crucial contest in this short, high-stakes series. With the T20 World Cup 2026 in India and Sri Lanka inching closer, every match is a stepping stone in shaping the ideal squad, refining strategies, and understanding player roles. Bangladesh ​​​​​​are leading the series by 1-0 after a dominant display in the first game, and a win today would give them the series with one match to spare. For Pakistan, this is about survival, a chance to bounce back, level things, and show that the first game was just a blip.
... MATCH DAY ...

The Shere Bangla National Stadium in Dhaka braces itself for Round Two of this three-match T20I showdown. With Bangladesh holding a 1-0 advantage after dismantling Pakistan in style, the buzz hasn’t been just about the cricket. The pitch at Mirpur has sparked controversy, most notably drawing flak from the head coach of Pakistan, Mike Hesson, who deemed it unworthy of an international contest, especially with the Asia Cup and next year’s T20 World Cup looming large. Yet, even Hesson couldn’t overlook Pakistan’s batting implosion, which went far beyond just surface-level woes. Missing a few key players, the tourists were clearly finding their feet in unfamiliar conditions. The adjustment wasn’t seamless, and even some of Pakistan’s experienced campaigners couldn’t quite hit their stride. With the series on the line, they'll be keen to regroup and respond. A loss here means Bangladesh takes the trophy, while a win keeps the contest alive, setting up a high-stakes third and final match where momentum will matter just as much as form. Pakistan’s collapse for 109 was their sixteenth-lowest total in T20Is and their third defeat in Dhaka. Fakhar Zaman was the lone bright spot in an otherwise dented top and middle order that struggled for momentum. Now, the spotlight shifts to the younger brigade. It’s a moment for talents like Saim Ayub and Mohammad Haris to take ownership and bring that raw, youthful intensity. If they can turn promise into performance, it could be a defining shift in Pakistan’s batting narrative. Losing one too many wickets early doors has a ripple effect. It forces the finishers to play anchor, upending the batting structure in a flash. That’s exactly the breakdown Pakistan found themselves navigating, and it's something they’ll want to avoid at all costs in the second contest. While the scoreboard didn’t offer the bowlers much cushion, they showed grit in return. One of the key takeaways was Salman Mirza’s spirited spell, offering both bite and promise. Yes, the absence of pace heavyweights like Haris Rauf, Shaheen Afridi, and Naseem Shah leaves a visible gap, but the youthful energy in this lineup carries its own intrigue. These fresh legs might lack experience, but they have the kind of unfiltered intent that could shift momentum. Bangladesh, since clinching that series win on Sri Lankan turf earlier this month, have barely put a foot wrong. They’ve continued to go after their opponents with intent, and this victory, which was their tenth biggest by wickets remaining and fifth largest by balls to spare, only reinforces their dominant run. Their top order has shown promising form lately, though the early stumble in the first match, losing two wickets inside ten runs, is a minor flaw they'll be looking to patch. With Tanzid, Litton, and Tawhid forming a potent trio, there's no shortage of firepower. What stands out, however, is the team’s collective ability to find a match-winner, someone who steps up and delivers that decisive blow, whether it’s with bat or ball. Taskin Ahmed led the bowling unit with conviction, setting the tone, and the rest followed with equal sincerity, ensuring the job was done without fuss. With the series delicately poised, it’s now or never for Pakistan and they surely will come spirited in this penultimate game. While Bangladesh will be aiming to extract all the help from their in-form squad. Come what may, it’s going to be a classic subcontinental rivalry.
